evidence_classes.OBSERVED-REPLICATED: Measured, and independently replicated across labs, datasets, or taxa. Carries a real citation, a falsifier, and the known range. Worked example (NA-00): the Schumann resonance fundamental, ~7.83 Hz — predicted by Schumann (1952), first extracted from background noise by Balser & Wagner (1960), Nature 188:638-641, measured at ELF stations worldwide since. Note what the class does NOT buy: it licenses the FREQUENCY, not any claim attached to the frequency.
evidence_classes.OBSERVED-CONTESTED: Measured, but the community genuinely disputes the value, the exponent, or the mechanism. BOTH POSITIONS MUST BE CARRIED AND THE DISPUTE NAMED. This is a feature, not an embarrassment. Worked example (NA-00): the metabolic scaling exponent b. Kleiber (1932) reported ~0.74; Dodds, Rothman & Weitz (2001) found little evidence for rejecting 2/3; White & Seymour (2003) report 0.686 +/- 0.014. The exponent MOVES WITH THE ANALYSIS CHOICES — which taxa are excluded, whether body temperature is normalised, whether the regression unit is the species or the order. That mobility IS the dispute, and a chapter that picks one number and drops the other has lied.
evidence_classes.MODELED: Derived from a model that fits data. THE MODEL'S ASSUMPTIONS ARE THE FENCE. Worked example (NA-00): West, Brown & Enquist (1997) derive b = 3/4 exactly, from three assumptions — a space-filling fractal branching network, terminal units invariant with body size, and minimised energy dissipation. The derivation is clean. It is also conditional: drop any one assumption and the 3/4 does not follow. Cite it as MODELED and cite the assumptions with it, or do not cite it.
evidence_classes.HYPOTHESIZED: Mechanism proposed, not settled. Not claimed. Worked example (NA-00): the radical-pair mechanism of avian magnetoreception (Ritz et al. 2000; PNAS DOI 10.1073/pnas.0711968106). Radio-frequency disruption experiments are consistent with it; much of the supporting evidence remains circumstantial, and a competing magnetite-based hypothesis is live. Birds navigate; HOW is not settled.
evidence_classes.INADMISSIBLE: A claim that failed observation, or that is unfalsifiable as stated. Carried WITH THE RECEIPT OF WHY IT FAILED. NEVER ASSERTED, NEVER MOCKED. Worked example (NA-00): '432 Hz is nature's true tuning.' A4 = 440 Hz is a CONVENTION — ISO 16:1975 fixes it at 440 +/- 0.5 Hz, not a natural constant — and 432 Hz is a different convention. Neither is more natural, and the claim names no measurand that could distinguish them. Inadmissible as physics or biology. THE PERSON ASKING IS NOT STUPID; THE CLAIM IS JUST NOT SHAPED LIKE A CLAIM YET.
evidence_classes.NOT-MEASURED: The honest empty face. Write this INSTEAD OF INVENTING A NUMBER. Worked example (NA-00): the effect size of the Schumann resonance on human physiology at ambient field strengths. The fields are in the PICOTESLA range. No pre-registered, independently replicated dose-response was found. THAT IS NOT A REFUTATION — IT IS AN ABSENCE, AND THE ABSENCE GETS WRITTEN DOWN AS AN ABSENCE.

nature_as_authority.doctrine: Nature is the authority because it is the only system that has ALREADY RUN THE EXPERIMENT — a very long parallel search, every lineage at once, under real physical constraints, in which THE FAILURES WERE DELETED. What remains is a heavily filtered sample of things that actually work, at real scales, on real energy budgets. That is a claim about SEARCH — not perfection, purpose, or wisdom. Nature is not an optimizer that found the best solution; it is a censor that removed a colossal number of bad ones. Survivors are ENRICHED FOR FEASIBILITY: exactly what makes them worth drawing hypotheses from, and exactly what does NOT make them right. Convergent evolution — independent lineages arriving at the same solution — is therefore evidence of a CONSTRAINT-OPTIMUM, and is the closest thing biology offers to a replicated experiment, with lineages as replicates. N = 1 IS A STORY. N = 62 IS A CONSTRAINT. The word doing all the work is INDEPENDENT, and it is the word most often abused.
nature_as_authority.mandatory_counterweight: Gould & Lewontin (1979), 'The spandrels of San Marco and the Panglossian paradigm: a critique of the adaptationist programme', Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 205(1161):581-598. NOT EVERY TRAIT IS AN ADAPTATION. Phylogenetic inertia, genetic drift, developmental constraint, pleiotropy, and historical contingency all produce features that are not optimal solutions to anything. An adaptive story can be told for anything; the ability to tell one is not evidence. THE WING'S TWO STANDING RECEIPTS: (1) THE VERTEBRATE INVERTED RETINA — our photoreceptors face AWAY from incoming light, which must cross the neural wiring to reach them, and the axon bundle punches back through the retina to exit, producing a BLIND SPOT. The cephalopod retina is EVERTED: photoreceptors face the light, axons exit behind, NO BLIND SPOT. Same problem, same regime, two lineages — and ONE IS WIRED BACKWARDS. Nature ran the experiment twice and shipped the worse design in us, because the developmental path could not be un-walked. (2) THE RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE — from the brain, DOWN past the aortic arch, back UP to the larynx. Wedel (2012) carries it to the limit: sauropod necks >10 m evolved independently in >=4 lineages; a 14 m neck implies RLN neurons >=28 m, possibly 40-50 m — plausibly the longest cells in the history of life, all to solve a routing problem that need not exist. IN BOTH, THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED THE TRAIT WAS HISTORY, NOT PHYSICS. COPY THEM AND YOU HAVE COPIED A SCAR.
nature_as_authority.operative_conclusion: 'NATURE DOES IT THIS WAY' IS A HYPOTHESIS GENERATOR, NEVER A PROOF. It earns a place on the candidate list, and nothing else. The biomimetic design must still beat a TUNED CONVENTIONAL BASELINE on a PRE-REGISTERED METRIC (repo rule M7), with a discriminator that COLLAPSES the gain if the stated mechanism is the real cause, and a true ablation — or it is recorded NEGATIVE. nature_as_authority.worked_pair: Oeffner & Lauder (2012), J. Exp. Biol. 215(5):785-795 — the rare study that measured the biology and the biomimetic product SIDE BY SIDE ON THE SAME RIG. THE SUCCESS HALF (principle copied): flexible REAL shark skin on a flapping foil swam +12.3% faster than the same foils after the denticles were sanded off. THE FAILURE HALF (form copied): the Speedo(R) Fastskin FS II fabric — marketed on the shark-skin analogy — showed NO consistent drag reduction; its V-shaped indentations ~1.25 mm apart DID NOT FUNCTION AS RIBLETS, and at 3 Hz the foil was SLOWER with the 'biomimetic' surface facing the water. IT WAS SHAPED LIKE THE ANSWER AND WAS NOT THE ANSWER. AND THE TWIST: on RIGID shark-skin plates, REMOVING the denticles IMPROVED performance — the opposite sign. Even the biological success is conditional: the benefit requires FLEXIBLE deformation, and the same structure on a stiff substrate is a LIABILITY. THE MECHANISM CARRIED THE RESULT. dimensionless_numbers.name: Reynolds number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of inertial to viscous forces
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Pipe transition: Re_c = 2040 ± 10 for the onset of SUSTAINED turbulence (Avila et al. 2011), where mean puff-decay time equals mean puff-splitting time; the textbook ~2300 (range ~2000–4000) answers a different question. Scope: smooth circular pipe only — it does not transfer to a wing or an artery.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Bacterium ~10⁻⁴–10⁻⁵ (Purcell 1977); man swimming ~10⁴; blue whale ~10⁸. Span bacterium→whale ≈ 10¹³ (~13 orders), NOT ~10¹⁰ (NA-10, corrected there).
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Re presumes you named the right L and u. A Re without a stated L is not a number.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Purcell (1977) Am J Phys 45:3–11; Avila et al. (2011) Science 333:192–196

dimensionless_numbers.name: Péclet number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of advection to diffusion
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Pe ≪ 1 → stirring is useless. Crossover: advection beats diffusion beyond L* = D/u (~30 µm for typical D and bacterial v).
dimensionless_numbers.example: Bacterium ~10⁻² (recomputed 3×10⁻²). To raise intake 10% a cell must swim 700 µm/s — ~20× faster than it can — because intake rises only as √v.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: D is species-specific. Pe for oxygen ≠ Pe for a protein in the same flow.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Damköhler number
dimensionless_numbers.formula: Da_I = k·τ (τ = residence time); Da_II = kL²/D
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of reaction rate to transport rate
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Da ≪ 1 → reaction-limited (stirring does nothing). Da ≫ 1 → transport-limited (the problem is delivery, not catalysis). Da ≈ 1 → both matter; model, don't estimate.
dimensionless_numbers.example: A cell with a fast enzyme (Da ≫ 1) and no circulation (Pe ≪ 1) starves no matter how good the enzyme is. Optimising the catalyst when the system is transport-limited is the most common design error at any scale.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Presumes one dominant reaction and one dominant transport path.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Froude number
dimensionless_numbers.formula: Fr = v²/(gL) — some authors use Fr = v/√(gL); one is the square of the other. A Froude number without its convention stated is defective.
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of inertial to gravitational forces; L = hip height (gait) or waterline length (hulls)
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Walk→run transition at Fr ≈ 0.5 — scoped to ADULT HUMANS AT 1 g. It FAILED off-Earth: in actual lunar gravity the measured transition was Fr = 1.39 ± 0.45, with 6 of 8 subjects choosing Fr > 1.0 (De Witt et al. 2014). The inverted-pendulum mechanical ceiling is Fr = 1.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Alexander's trackway formula, u = 0.25·g^0.5·λ^1.67·h^(−1.17) with h ≈ 4× footprint length, gives dinosaur speeds 1.0–3.6 m/s. TESTED AND PARTLY REFUTED: on mud, against n=2 helmeted guineafowl, calculated speed ran 1.17–4.74× measured, typically ~2× (Prescott et al. 2025).
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Fr similarity assumes gravity-dominated dynamics and geometric similarity. It says nothing about elastic storage — Fr cannot see a kangaroo's tendon spring.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Alexander (1976) Nature 261:129–130; Alexander (1983) J. Zool.; De Witt et al. (2014) JEB 217:3200–3203; Prescott et al. (2025) Biol Lett 21:20250191

dimensionless_numbers.name: Strouhal number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of oscillatory to forward speed; f = beat frequency, A = peak-to-peak amplitude, U = cruise speed
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: 0.2 < St < 0.4 AT CRUISE — the band of high propulsive efficiency (Taylor, Nudds & Thomas 2003). Scope is the science: not takeoff, not manoeuvre, not hovering. Individual scatter is large — only 44% of 248 odontocete values fall in 0.225–0.275 (Rohr & Fish 2004). Eloy (2012) models the OPTIMAL St as size-dependent, rising 0.15 → 0.8 from the largest cetaceans to the smallest tadpoles.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Water-walkers occupy a DIFFERENT band: 0.1 < St < 1 (large), 0.01 < St < 0.1 (arthropods) — Bush & Hu 2006. Glossophaga soricina bats measure St = 0.17–0.22 near minimum-power speed, slightly BELOW the canonical 0.2 bound.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Presumes steady cruise; silent about unsteady manoeuvre. The band describes where animals cruise; it is not a law they obey.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Taylor, Nudds & Thomas (2003) Nature 425:707–711; Bush & Hu (2006) ARFM 38:339–369; Rohr & Fish (2004) JEB 207:1633–1642; Eloy (2012) J Fluids Struct 30:205–218

dimensionless_numbers.name: Womersley number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of transient (oscillatory) inertia to viscous shear
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: α ≫ 1 (aorta ≈13.2, some studies ≈20.3): inertia-dominated, blunt plug-like profile lagging the pressure gradient. α ≪ 1 (capillary ≈0.005; all microcirculation < 1): quasi-steady, Poiseuille-like, parabolic and in phase — the capillary does not know the heart is beating.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Same fluid, same pump, two regimes, one number.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Assumes a Newtonian fluid in a rigid tube. Blood is shear-thinning, vessels are compliant, and in capillaries the red cell is comparable to the vessel diameter — continuum blood is arguably the wrong model there entirely.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Weber number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of inertia to surface tension; σ = surface tension (air–water ≈ 0.07 N/m), w = leg width
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: We < 1 → the driving leg's meniscus survives — satisfied by all water-walking insects APART FROM the galloping fisher spider (carry the exception, it is real). Bush & Hu report the fit Bo ∼ We across water walkers.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Water striders: characteristic length 1 cm, weight 10 dynes (10⁻⁴ N). Required leg contact length L = W/σ = 10⁻⁴/0.07 ≈ 1.4 mm — trivially available on a 1 cm insect.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: σ collapses with surfactant. A drop of detergent sinks a strider — also the cleanest falsification test of the whole account.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Bush & Hu (2006) ARFM 38:339–369; Hu, Chan & Bush (2003) Nature 424:663–666

dimensionless_numbers.name: Bond (Eötvös) number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of gravity to surface tension
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Bo < 1 → supported by surface tension. The capillary length is the crossover: ℓ_c = (σ/ρg)^(1/2) ≈ 2.6 mm (CN-02 recomputes 2.71 mm at 25 °C). Below it, surface tension dominates gravity; above it, gravity wins.
dimensionless_numbers.example: This is why an insect's world and a human's world are different worlds. Water-walking insects weigh no more than 1–10 dynes with body perimeter ~1 cm, so crossing the air–water interface would require forces of order 10–100 TIMES THEIR WEIGHT. The surface is not a nuisance to an insect — it is a wall.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: σ collapses with surfactant.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Knudsen number
dimensionless_numbers.formula: Kn = λ/L; λ ≈ 68 nm for air at 1 atm, 25 °C
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of molecular mean free path to system size — where 'fluid' stops being a fluid
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Gas flows: continuum Kn < 0.01 (Navier–Stokes, no-slip); slip 0.01–0.1 (N–S usable IF slip boundary conditions are added); transition 0.1–10 (kinetic theory required); free-molecular > 10 (molecules collide only with walls).
dimensionless_numbers.example: An alveolus is ~200 µm: Kn ≈ 3.4×10⁻⁴ → continuum; deep-lung air is an ordinary fluid. But a 100 nm aerosol particle in that SAME alveolus sees Kn ≈ 0.7 → transition regime, where Stokes drag is wrong without the Cunningham slip correction. Same air, same lung, two regimes — because Kn depends on the L you are asking about, not on the fluid.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: A gas concept. Liquids have no comparable mean free path.
dimensionless_numbers.source: standard rarefied-gas references; standard kinetic theory

dimensionless_numbers.name: Deborah number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of the material's relaxation time to your observation time
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: De ≫ 1 → BEHAVES AS a solid. De ≪ 1 → BEHAVES AS a liquid. Not 'appears to' — behaves as.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Pitch, silly putty, glacial ice, the Earth's mantle (viscosity 10²¹ poise) — each is solid or liquid depending entirely on how long you watch. The mantle is a solid to a seismic wave and a fluid to a continent. This is the earned, rigorous version of 'everything depends on the timescale'; without the ratio it is a slogan. Solid and liquid are not properties of a material at all — they are properties of the PAIRING of a material with an observation timescale.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Presumes a SINGLE dominant relaxation time. Real polymers and tissues have a broad relaxation spectrum; one De is then a summary, not a description.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Reiner (1964) Physics Today 17(1):62, doi 10.1063/1.3051374; mantle viscosity quoted in Purcell (1977)

dimensionless_numbers.name: Prandtl number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of momentum to thermal diffusivity
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Pr ≪ 1 → heat outruns momentum; thermal boundary layer THICKER than the velocity layer.
dimensionless_numbers.example: 7 (water), 0.71 (air), 0.025 (mercury), near room temperature.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Property values are condition-dependent.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Schmidt number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of momentum to mass diffusivity — Prandtl's mass-transfer twin
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Sc ≫ 1 in liquids: momentum spreads far faster than solute.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Pr's mass-transfer twin.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: D is species-specific.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Nusselt number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of total to conductive heat transfer
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Nu = 1 → pure conduction, no convective benefit.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Nu is the ANSWER you measure, not an input.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: k is the FLUID's in Nu (contrast Biot, where k is the solid's). Confusing them is a classic error.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Sherwood number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of total to diffusive mass transfer — Nusselt's twin
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Sphere in stagnant fluid: Sh = 2 — the diffusion-limited floor that Purcell's 4πaND expresses.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Nu's twin.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Grashof number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of buoyancy to viscous forces — free convection's Reynolds number
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Gr/Re² ≫ 1 → buoyancy dominates forced flow.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Free convection's Re.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Rayleigh number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of buoyancy to diffusive damping
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Ra_c = 1707.762 (rigid–rigid boundaries), critical wavenumber ≈ 3.117, INDEPENDENT OF Pr AT ONSET. Below it, no convection; above it, Bénard cells.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Rayleigh–Bénard convection onset.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Ra_c is boundary-condition specific (the quoted value is rigid–rigid).

dimensionless_numbers.name: Biot number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of internal conductive to surface resistance
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Bi < 0.1 → lumped-capacitance admissible. MODELED: an engineering convention, not a law.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Bi and Nu look identical: k is the SOLID's in Bi, the FLUID's in Nu. Confusing them is a classic error.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: A convention, not a law.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Mach number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of flow speed to sound speed
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Ma < 0.3 → density change <~5%, incompressible admissible (a convention). Ma = 1 → shocks.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Sets the validity band for matched-Re air/water comparisons (CN-03's falsifier is scoped to Mach ≪ 1).
dimensionless_numbers.limit: A convention, not a law.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Rossby number
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of inertial to Coriolis forces — whether rotation matters at all
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Ro ≈ 0.1 → rotation DOMINATES → geostrophic balance, which is the whole reason weather maps work: pressure-gradient and Coriolis forces nearly balance, so wind blows ALONG isobars rather than across them. Ro ≫ 1 → rotation irrelevant. Inside the Hadley cells the vorticity-based LOCAL Rossby number is order 1 — a different definition and a different regime.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Midlatitude weather system (U=10 m/s, L=1,000 km): Ro = 0.097 → rotation dominates. Tornado (U=50 m/s, L=100 m): Ro ≈ 4.8×10³ → rotation IRRELEVANT. Draining sink (U=0.01 m/s, L=0.3 m): Ro ≈ 3×10² → rotation irrelevant, ~300× too weak to compete with the residual circulation already in the basin. BUT the physics is real and was measured: Shapiro (1962) used a covered 6-ft tank and let it settle 24 HOURS to drive U→0 — the only regime where the effect can win — and saw the rotation. The 24-hour settle is not fussiness, it IS the experiment.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Ro depends on the definition used (bulk vs vorticity-based); the Hadley 'local Ro' is a different quantity from the synoptic one.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Golden angle (phyllotactic divergence)
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: dimensionless divergence angle; the attractor of repulsion-driven sequential primordia
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Clusters near 137.5° in spiral-phyllotactic vascular plants — but NOT universal: in the largest sunflower study with explicit inclusion criteria, 18% of scored counts (136/768) were NON-Fibonacci (Swinton & Ochu 2016). Scope: the attractor at LOW control parameter G — the same experiment yields OTHER angles at other G.
dimensionless_numbers.example: THE WING'S TEMPLATE FOR EARNED VS UNEARNED. Douady & Couder (1992) reproduced it in a PHYSICAL ferrofluid-droplet experiment: droplets polarised into dipoles repel and drift outward; the divergence angle converges on the golden mean because that value AVOIDS rational (periodic) organisation, i.e. avoids collisions with earlier primordia. No genes, no selection, no mysticism — mechanism, physical realisation, and a knob you can turn to break it. The number is not the evidence; the MECHANISM is the evidence.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: The mechanism that earns 137.5° in a sunflower earns nothing in a spiral galaxy or a nautilus shell unless THAT mechanism is shown to operate THERE. See inadmissible: 'the golden ratio is a universal design law of nature'.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Douady & Couder (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 68(13):2098–2101, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.2098; Swinton & Ochu (2016) R. Soc. Open Sci. 3:160091

dimensionless_numbers.name: Drag anisotropy ratio (resistive-force theory)
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: ratio of normal to tangential drag on a slender filament — the asymmetry that makes flagellar thrust possible at all
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: ≈2 ASYMPTOTIC ONLY; ~1.5–1.8 at realistic aspect ratios (ln(2λ/a) ≈ 3–5). Strictly < 2 for any real filament; reaches 2 only as aspect ratio → ∞. Set the ratio to 1 and thrust integrates to ZERO — travelling wave or not.
dimensionless_numbers.example: The entire propulsion of every flagellate on Earth is bought from an order-1.5-to-2 asymmetry in the drag on a thin rod.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: A derived slender-body Stokes coefficient, NOT a measurement. Slenderness is the fence.

dimensionless_numbers.name: Buckingham Pi theorem
dimensionless_numbers.formula: Number of groups = n − j, where j = the RANK of the dimensional matrix (NOT the number of base dimensions — that is the common failure mode, and it is wrong whenever the dimensions are not independently represented). Then Π₁ = f(Π₂, …, Π_{n−j}).
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: the recipe for generating your OWN dimensionless groups
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: Worked example — drag on a sphere: variables F, ρ, U, D, μ; n = 5, rank j = 3 → 2 groups. Π₁ = F/(ρU²D²) → drag coefficient C_d; Π₂ = μ/(ρUD) → 1/Re. Result: C_d = f(Re). Five variables collapse to one curve.
dimensionless_numbers.example: THE FENCE, PRINTED WHERE IT HURTS: that took ten minutes and it did NOT hand you f. Nothing in Buckingham's theorem predicts C_d ≈ 0.5 in the subcritical range, or that near Re ≈ 3×10⁵ smooth-sphere drag FALLS ~5× as the boundary layer trips turbulent and the wake narrows — the drag crisis. That is why golf balls have dimples, and dimensional analysis could never have told you. Only the experiment found it.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: Step 1 (list all n relevant variables) is the whole game and is NOT mathematics — it is physics judgment. Omit a relevant variable and every group downstream is wrong.
dimensionless_numbers.source: Buckingham (1914) Physical Review 4(4):345–376, doi 10.1103/PhysRev.4.345 (not first: Vaschy 1892; Federman and Riabouchinsky 1911 have priority)

dimensionless_numbers.name: Dynamic similarity and the conflict you cannot escape
dimensionless_numbers.formula: Fr matching requires v_m = v_s·√λ (model goes SLOWER); Re matching requires v_m = v_s/λ (model goes FASTER)
dimensionless_numbers.meaning: geometrically similar systems sharing every relevant group have identical dimensionless results — but you can rarely match all groups at once
dimensionless_numbers.critical_values: At scale λ = 1/25: v_m = 0.2·v_s versus v_m = 25·v_s. INCOMPATIBLE BY A FACTOR OF 125. No cleverness removes this.
dimensionless_numbers.example: Froude's hypothesis, stated as the assumption it is: split resistance into a wave-making (residuary) part governed by Fr and a frictional part governed by Re; run at matched Fr, estimate the model's friction from a flat-plate correlation (e.g. the ITTC-1957 line) at the MODEL's Re and subtract, scale the residuary remainder by Fr, add back FULL-SCALE friction at FULL-SCALE Re.
dimensionless_numbers.limit: MODELED, and its assumptions are the fence: that the two components are independent and additive (they are not, strictly — the boundary layer alters the wave field), and that a flat plate is an acceptable friction proxy for a hull. It works well enough to build ships. It is not a law.
dimensionless_numbers.source: NA-07 'Dynamic similarity — and the conflict you cannot escape'
